candidate_relations.reason: The biopsy shows foamy histiocytes packed with acid-fast bacilli rather than an atypical cutaneous lymphocytic infiltrate.
Although lymph nodes and spleen are enlarged, the organism-rich dermal histiocytic infiltrate and diffuse facial involvement support infection rather than lymphoma.
Numerous acid-fast bacilli in the nodules are incompatible with sarcoidosis as the unifying diagnosis.
The case has no auricular, nasal, or airway chondritis and instead demonstrates multibacillary skin disease.
Uveitis on fluorescein angiography is one organ manifestation accompanying the systemic leprosy reaction.
Even if the reported uveitis is granulomatous, it does not encompass the bacillary dermal disease, alopecia, nodules, and arthritis.
There are no sicca symptoms or Sjögren serologies, while acid-fast organisms are abundant in a skin lesion.
Leprosy identifies the bacillary infection but omits the lepromatous pole and the type 2 reaction causing systemic inflammation.
Lupus vulgaris is a paucibacillary tuberculosis form, unlike the diffuse foamy histiocytes containing numerous acid-fast bacilli in this case.
The patient has no psoriasis and has multiorgan findings including bacilli-laden nodules, lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and uveitis.
The diffuse facial infiltration, hair loss, foamy histiocytes, and heavy bacillary load establish lepromatous leprosy, but this label omits the reactional state.
Granulomatous disease is too broad to retain the demonstrated acid-fast etiology, lepromatous subtype, and type 2 reaction.
Lupus pernio would not account for numerous acid-fast bacilli in dermal foamy histiocytes or the leprosy-associated alopecia.
Granuloma annulare does not produce diffuse facial infiltration, systemic lymphoid enlargement, or an organism-rich biopsy.
Normal antinuclear antibodies and the positive acid-fast stain argue against lupus as the cause of the nodules and arthritis.
Erythema nodosum leprosum is the type 2 leprosy reaction that explains the tender inflammatory systemic features but does not by itself specify the underlying lepromatous infection.
The arm nodules could resemble erythema nodosum clinically, but biopsy instead shows dermal foamy histiocytes with many acid-fast bacilli.
Elevated rheumatoid factor and erosive synovitis are misleading because anti-CCP is normal and concurrent bacillary skin disease and uveitis provide a different systemic cause.
Necrobiosis lipoidica does not match the diffuse foamy histiocytic infiltrate with abundant acid-fast bacilli.
A heavy acid-fast burden alone does not make tuberculosis, while the madarosis, leonine facial infiltration, and lepromatous histology form a characteristic leprosy pattern.
